title: Lorenzo Tio, the Tio family and Guy Kelly
summary: Discussion of Tio's uneven playing and nickname Lazy Mexican, whether the family came from Mexico, and Guy (Edgar) Kelly's playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Tio himself, uh, had about two styles, didn't he, that he used? Two distinct styles of Tio. Tio?
Yeah. Oh, yeah. Yeah, Tio.
I mean, some of the styles we heard on the records wasn't the kind he played all the time, was it?
No. Well, he played caught in the high field. Oh, yeah. Caught in the high field. If he was feeling good, he played good. If he was, if he just feel bad, he...
Yeah, I guess a lot of people are that way. Yeah.
You had to catch him caught in the high field. That's why we used to call him Lazy Mexican.
Oh, yeah.
Cause he played caught in the East field. We used to call him Lazy Mexican for a nickname.
Do you know if that family came from Mexico really or not? Did they...
Well, really I could not say that. Mm-hmm.
Some people have told me that the old man, uh, Louie Tio and, uh, Lorenzo Senior came from Mexico.
Well, I'll tell you who, who, who should be able to tell you about that. Manu Mineta should be able to tell you about that.
He didn't seem to remember for sure. He played with the Papa Tio too at the Tuxedo Band too. Yeah. Four year time he even played there I think. Oh, yeah. He didn't remember they came from Mexico.
He can't remember that part back.
But, uh, Mr. Paul Goliere, you know. Yeah, he should know too. He said he thought they came from Mexico. He studied with the Tio.

Well, if he told you, well... He should know. Well, he should know, yeah. Yeah. His sister used to teach me, you know. I said, take lessons, I'll just go to... We call him Guy Kelly, but his right name is Edgar Kelly. Guy Kelly.
That wasn't Spider.
No, that's not Spider. That's two different man talk.
Everyone ever talks about Spider said he was really good on the jump stuff.

Yeah, yeah. Well, that's what I'm talking about. Yeah. He wasn't much of a musician. Yeah. You know what I mean? He could play it. Now, don't get me wrong. Yeah, yeah. He could play it, but I mean his reading ability wasn't so far. He could play. All right, nobody tell you he couldn't play. He really could play.
